title: Compliance gating flow for sensitivity-tiering and accelerated evidence paths
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit varied security/compliance asks (SOC2 evidence requests, vendor questionnaires, DPA terms, GDPR data subject questions, HIPAA scoping) through multiple channels. Current handling is ad-hoc, inconsistent SLAs, and engineering/legal/solutions get duplicated work. This ticket will define and ship a deterministic 'compliance gate' that maps incoming asks into sensitivity tiers, recommended evidence bundles, SLA lanes, and an exception lifecycle with audit logging. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-response, eliminate repeated evidence retrieval, and provide a clear audit trail for audits (SOC2/ISO) and customer reviewers.

Scope: policy + config + lightweight automation only (no full LLM autopilot). Deliverables: classification rules + human-in-loop review UI, tier -> evidence bundle catalog, SLA lane definitions, routing rules (Security, Legal, Solutions, Support), exception templates (DPA variance, HIPAA scoping), and observability dashboards. Integration points: Zendesk/Support form, Customer Portal, Confluence evidence store, GitHub ticketing for engineering work, and existing Console 'Requests' dashboard.

Out of scope: full vendor-questionnaire auto-completion, end-to-end legal negotiations (we provide templates & handoff), deep ML model training beyond prototype classifier.
user_story: As a product manager supporting enterprise customers, I want incoming security/compliance asks to be automatically assigned a sensitivity tier and matched to a recommended evidence bundle so that support/security/legal can respond faster with consistent quality and we can track SLAs for audits.
acceptance_criteria: All new security/compliance requests submitted via the support form or account executive intake are classified into Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 with >85% accuracy in pilot and clear human override path
Each tier is associated with a standardized evidence bundle (links to Confluence/Drive) and a target SLA (Tier 1: 48 hours, Tier 2: 5 business days, Tier 3: 15 business days)
Routing rules send requests to the correct owner queue (Support, Security Ops, Legal, Solutions) with automatic flags for DPA/HIPAA/GDPR scope questions
Exceptions (contract variance, data residency blocks) generate a template DPA exception doc and an escalated task with required stakeholders pre-populated
Console dashboard surfaces queue backlog, average time-to-first-response, evidence completeness %, and audit log of decision provenance (rule/classifier + reviewer + timestamp)
Security and Legal have reviewed and approved audit logging requirements and evidence catalog linking format
updates: 2026-03-05: PRD draft completed and shared with Security and Legal. Initial sensitivity-tier taxonomy proposed (Tier 1: non-sensitive config/labels, Tier 2: customer data processing + APIs, Tier 3: regulated PHI/PII/contractual residency). Link to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENT/Compliance+Gate+PRD

2026-03-06: Scoping call with Support and Solutions. Agreed to require 1-click human override in the intake UI and to store evidence links in a single canonical Confluence folder. Action: Solutions to curate evidence bundles (owner: Maya Chen, due 2026-03-20).

2026-03-08: Engineering feasibility sync. Eng raised concerns about audit log retention and access controls for Private deployments; Security Ops requested logs to be available for 90 days by default and exportable for SOC2 review. Created engineering spike ENG-21455 to prototype audit export endpoint (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/issues/ENG-21455).

2026-03-09: Legal provided DPA exception template and approved exception escalation path. Legal requested metadata capture: requester, account id, question id, evidence links, reviewer, and final disposition. Legal also requested a POA (point of authority) field for contract exceptions.

2026-03-10: Decision: build rule-based classifier for MVP (pattern match + keyword heuristics + form fields) instead of ML model to accelerate rollout. ML classifier deferred to follow-up (PM-501238). Next: wireframe intake UI, finalize tier definitions, and schedule pilot with top 5 enterprise customers for 2026-03-28.
